_doc: Owner feedback 8 (W14, W2) — stream C, js/rules/projectiles.js. Every ranged attack is a projectile that TRAVELS: the damage is dealt when it arrives. Farhold flew a skill bolt at 48 m/s, an arrow at 42 and a monster's shot at 40 — at fighting distance that is 4 to 6 frames, which read as 'instant damage' and 'I was hit and never saw from where'. These are the speeds (metres a second) a flight is worked out from; `minMs` is the shortest flight there is. A projectile HOMES: it lands on its target wherever the target stands when it arrives; a target that died on the way is not replaced (the shot strikes the ground where it fell). `skill.byId` wins over `skill.byElement` over `skill.default`; `basic` is a weapon's own attack by its type (items.json `subtype`); `monster` is a monster's ranged attack by element. `proj` is what the client draws (D-world's list: arrow, quarrel, knife, axe, javelin, stone, firebolt, orb, shard). A parity engine (tests) has no table and keeps Farhold's speeds and its aimed-at-a-point arrows.
